title: The Bondage of Sin
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The bondage of sin means that sin enslaves fallen people, corrupting desires, ruling choices, and keeping sinners from freedom apart from God’s grace. Sin is not merely a mistake to correct; it is a master from which sinners need deliverance.
summary: The bondage of sin means that sin enslaves fallen people, corrupting desires, ruling choices, and keeping sinners from freedom apart from God’s grace. Sin is not merely a mistake to correct; it is a master from which sinners need deliverance.
christFocus: Jesus Christ came to set captives free from sin’s guilt, power, and dominion. Through His death and resurrection, believers are no longer slaves of sin but are brought under the gracious lordship of Christ.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture describes sin as more than wrong actions. Sin enslaves. It rules desires, deceives the mind, hardens the heart, and brings people under its power. People may think they are free while they are being mastered by what destroys them.

The bondage of sin is seen in repeated patterns of rebellion, addiction, bitterness, lust, pride, fear, hatred, greed, unbelief, and idolatry. A person may hate the consequences of sin while still being drawn back to its false promises.

This bondage cannot be broken by human strength alone. Sinners need deliverance, not merely advice. They need Christ to forgive guilt, break sin’s dominion, give new life, and bring them into the freedom of serving God.

Believers still battle sin, but they are no longer under sin’s rightful mastery. In Christ, they have died to sin’s reign and been raised to walk in newness of life. Freedom is not the ability to do whatever the flesh wants; freedom is belonging to Christ and living unto God.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people understand sin only as a series of bad decisions, so they assume the answer is simply more discipline, more shame, or more effort. But bondage requires deliverance. A chained person does not need decoration; he needs to be set free.

This doctrine speaks directly to addiction, hidden sin, destructive patterns, and long-term spiritual struggle. It tells the truth about sin’s power without denying the greater power of Christ. No bondage is stronger than the Savior who frees sinners and teaches them to walk in new life.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not make peace with the sin that Christ died to break. Bring bondage into the light before God, confess it honestly, and seek the help of Scripture, prayer, the Spirit, and faithful believers. Fight sin from your new position in Christ, not from despair. Freedom grows as you turn from sin’s false promises and live under the gracious rule of Jesus.
